correctness.rationale: Conditional vertex ages are iid min(Exp(1),u), and edge indicators are independent given the age vector with probabilities \(1-\exp[-c\min(X_i,X_j)/(N-1)]\). The giant criterion follows from BJR Theorem 3.1 on the fixed-time bounded irreducible kernel. The moments \(m_1=(1-e^{-2u})/2\) and \(m_2=(1-3e^{-2u}+2e^{-3u})/3\) are exactly the degree-only closure inputs. The minimum kernel is compact, injective and positive semidefinite, so strict \(m_2<\|K\|m_1\) follows because \(K\mathbf1=1-e^{-x}\) is not constant. Its principal eigenfunction solves the stated ODE and endpoint-atom Robin condition, giving the finite-time Bessel determinant. Coupled kernels give strict time monotonicity and stationary \(j_{0,1}^2/4\). The standalone verification script completed 42 symbolic/numeric assertions, supplementing the proof.

originality.rationale: The printed degree-based finite-time threshold in Artime (arXiv:2211.01869, Eq. 16) is genuinely different from the corrected phase boundary derived from the full age-conditioned graph law. The strict all-u gap and the Robin Bessel condition induced by the finite-time endpoint atom are not stated in the inspected sources. The generic inhomogeneous-graph phase criterion and the stationary Bessel constant are known from Bollobás–Janson–Riordan (arXiv:math/0504589); the specific transient correction, not those ingredients, is the assessed contribution. Implicit priority risk remains.
residual_risks: General inhomogeneous-graph theory and the stationary Bessel constant are prior art; the originality assessment is restricted to the atom-sensitive transient correction to Artime’s stated model.
An overlooked prior calculation for the same truncated-exponential age measure or a publication correcting Artime’s finite-time threshold could supersede the new contribution.
The result does not address a joint long-time and large-N scaling window or finite-size threshold fluctuations.

value.rationale: The theorem corrects a published all-time percolation phase criterion in a natural resetting-network process, establishing for every positive time a nonempty interval of genuine giant-component emergence misclassified by degree-only analysis. The endpoint atom changes the spectral boundary in a nontrivial way; the explicit Bessel relation and strict operator inequality make the correction global rather than a numerical spot check. The stationary constant is properly attributed to existing work.
